tb21_profile.skill: Know the QEMU CLI well enough to redirect the guest's serial console to a listening TCP socket (-serial telnet:127.0.0.1:6665,server), launch the VM detached, and poll until the login prompt is actually being served before returning
tb21_profile.domain: QEMU system emulation, Alpine ISO boot, serial console / telnet, background process management on Linux
tb21_profile.task_form: configure-a-service: leave a long-lived daemon running and block on a readiness condition; graded by an expect script that connects and looks for the login prompt

searches: tools.py search all 'until it(.s| is) ready|wait until|poll.{0,30}(port|until)|in the background and leave|nohup|run in the background' -n 30
tools.py search rebench 'bind.{0,20}port|listen on|daemon|start the server|127\.0\.0\.1:|subprocess|background process|docker|container' -n 30

TMax-15K.reason: Automate the interactive QEMU monitor exposed on a socket using pexpect. Talking to a QEMU console over a socket is the whole TB task.
Launch QEMU VMs with port forwarding and poll every second until a readiness marker appears before proceeding. QEMU plus block-until-ready, together.
Start a QEMU VM in the background from a script and guarantee it is still running after the script exits, with a service inside reachable.
Compose the qemu-system invocation with machine type, drive, display and -netdev user; exactly the flag vocabulary needed to expose a console.
Generate the precise qemu-system-x86_64 command line (VNC display, netdev, hostfwd, fw_cfg); teaches how QEMU character/network backends are spelled.
Provision disks, launch QEMU VMs and run connectivity diagnostics against the running guest, all unprivileged. Launch-and-verify loop.
A service that answers only an interactive TCP login prompt; must script a probe that connects and works the prompt. The grader's expect script, inverted.
Get a running QEMU VM reachable from the host on a chosen local port and keep the connection alive for a grader to use.
Drive a text-based appliance shell with pexpect: wait for its prompt, send configuration, dump the result. Console automation without a TTY.
Parse and validate QEMU startup configurations including hostfwd and -virtfs; forces real understanding of QEMU's command-line grammar.

Recursive-Task-Synthesis.reason: Connect to a host over telnet, log in as root at the prompt and drive it. The client half of what this TB task must make possible.
Define a VM, including its virtualisation options, that is meant to be booted under QEMU. Same target hypervisor, declarative instead of CLI.
Start a server then wait until it is actually serving before proceeding; the readiness-polling discipline the 'block until it's ready' clause demands.
Start a daemon on a port, poll its health endpoint until it reports healthy, and record the live PID and listening port. Same start-then-confirm shape.
Script that starts the server, polls the endpoint until it returns the expected payload, then exits successfully. Readiness loop in a shell script.
Assemble a boot command with kernel, initrd and console=ttyS0,115200; serial-console boot parameters are how a headless guest talks at all.
Start a daemon that is installed but not running and wait until it answers its ping endpoint before initialising it.
Start a netcat listener on a fixed port, keep it running, and capture its process and listening-socket state as evidence.
Start a container and wait until the server inside it accepts connections before issuing commands; boot-then-wait against a slow guest.
Build a QEMU-bootable NixOS VM with a user and automatic login, so the console is usable the moment it comes up.

TerminalWorld-Seeds-Clean.reason: Run a guest command under the QEMU i386 system emulator and capture its console output, then replay it. Direct qemu-system operation.
Connect to a telnet login service as root with no password and capture what the session prints. Exactly the connection the grader will make.
Build a qcow2 overlay over a base image and boot the VM with injected seed config so it comes up ready to be used.
Generate a seed image and boot a downloaded cloud image locally with it; booting an unmodified OS image under a hypervisor and getting it usable.
Import an image and start a VM from a JSON definition; provision-and-boot-a-guest with explicit device configuration.
Download a cloud image, resize it and boot the VM with cloud-init so its console login works. Same boot-an-image-until-you-can-log-in goal.
Bootstrap an Alpine root filesystem with static apk-tools, mount proc/sys/dev and enter it. Alpine internals behind the ISO being booted.
Write a complete VM configuration whose output artifact is runnable under QEMU; specifying a guest that must actually boot.
Leave a guest running detached with a host port mapped onto its login service, so an external client can connect. Same end-state contract.
Install a server, start it on its port, then query it over the network to prove it is up; start-a-daemon-and-probe-it, no virtualisation.

SWE-Smith-Seeds-Clean.reason: ProxyCommand's send/recv mishandle bytes and empty payloads; piping a session through an external process, like a console bridged to a socket.
Worker spawning breaks when os.fork() returns 0 in the child; reasoning about detaching a process correctly, which backgrounding QEMU needs.
Server refuses to start unless every binding option is explicit; debugging why a daemon never comes up and never listens.
Socket creation from an address configuration fails with a TypeError; getting a daemon to bind the intended host:port is the graded condition here too.
parse_address stops rejecting malformed tcp://host:port strings; precise reasoning about listen-address syntax and its silent failures.
Arbiter unlinks listening sockets at the wrong times on shutdown; lifecycle of a long-lived listener across parent and child processes.
Workers fail to initialise: env not set, sockets not added to wait_fds, uid/gid swapped. Classic why-won't-my-daemon-come-up debugging.
Opening an interactive session channel over a transport breaks; the channel-to-a-remote-shell abstraction the telnet console stands in for.
Stale unix socket files left behind after shutdown; cleaning up listener endpoints so a restarted daemon can bind again.
Worker processes are not cleaned up on exit and systemd socket handling is wrongly on by default; process-supervision correctness.

SWE-Rebench-Tasks-Clean.reason: Awaiting an ssh subprocess loses the result object; launching an external long-running command from code and reading what it emits.
A daemon thread's join(timeout) races against startup; the wait-until-it-is-actually-up problem in miniature.
Connection upgrade to a raw bidirectional stream (docker exec) regressed; hijacking a socket to reach a container's console.
Host:port parsing breaks when a scheme prefix is present; the same address-string care a -serial telnet:127.0.0.1:6665 spec needs.
A long-running daemon's disconnect handler loops retrying mid-run; debugging a background service that is supposed to stay up.
run-instances rejects a valid launch flag; validating the parameter set that starts a virtual machine, albeit an emulated cloud one.
Reproduction requires two real interfaces plus iptables; reasoning about which local address a connection binds to and leaves from.
ssh:// path handling changed between versions; parsing user@host:port style locators correctly.
Inconsistent password handling in load_ssh_private_key; same remote-access ecosystem, nothing about starting or reaching a service.
Bug reproduced against a server container with a host port published; port publishing is scaffolding, not the problem being solved.

Run a guest command under the QEMU i386 system emulator and capture its console output; direct qemu-system driving, not a wrapper tool.
Compose the qemu-system invocation with machine type, drive, display and netdev backends; the flag vocabulary needed to expose a console.
Generate the exact qemu-system-x86_64 command line with display and network backends; teaches how QEMU character backends are spelled.
A service reachable only through an interactive TCP login prompt; script a probe that connects and works the prompt. The grader's expect script, inverted.
Connect to a telnet login service as root with no password and capture the session output. Precisely the connection the verifier makes.
Provision disks, launch QEMU VMs and then run connectivity diagnostics against the guest; the launch-then-verify loop, unprivileged.
Connect over telnet, log in as root at the console prompt and drive the machine; the client half of what this task must make possible.

notes: Sister task to qemu-alpine-ssh; the overlap in TMax QEMU candidates is deliberate, but I reweighted toward the two skills this one actually needs and the other does not: exposing a console over a socket (task_003288's QEMU monitor over a UNIX socket is the single best match in the pool) and blocking on a readiness condition (task_000021 polls until ready; several RTS tasks do the same against HTTP servers). Retrieval was poor here: TMax rank 1 (task_000146, 4/4 retrievers) is OCR-a-config-image plus a webhook receiver with nothing in common, and most of the top-20 are 'extract config from an image then start a service' tasks that match on the service-startup boilerplate only; the real QEMU tasks were at rank 21 and scattered through rest_ids. Recursive-Task-Synthesis's biggest cluster for this query is figlet banner rendering, a pure token collision on 'banner' and 'prompt' - all rejected. SWE-Rebench again has nothing: no document in it starts a VM or serves a console, so the whole list caps at overall 2 and I chose on daemon-lifecycle and address-parsing skill alone. SWE-Smith is gunicorn (listener binding, fork/detach, socket cleanup) plus paramiko; also no genre match.
